newsitem.title: FRANCE: Talk of who should head ECB premature - France.
newsitem.headline: Talk of who should head ECB premature - France.

text.p: French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said on Wednesday discussion about who should head the future European central Bank (ECB) was "premature".

Speaking to reporters after a cabinet meeting, Lamassoure said France had agreed to the appointment of Dutch central bank governor Wim Duisenberg as head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), forerunner of the future ECB.
As regards who will head the ECB, Lamassoure said, "it's a problem which will arise later, it's premature".
The French government dismissed newspaper reports on Tuesday it had proposed International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus, a Frenchman, as head of the ECB.
But it restated France's position that who will get the post remains an open question.

Presidential spokeswoman Catherine Colonna reiterated on Tuesday the official French position that the decision to make Duisenberg head of the EMI did not mean he would automatically become head of the ECB.
